title: Diwali 2026: India's Best Places to Experience the Festival of Lights
excerpt: From a million diyas on Varanasi's ghats to the Golden Temple mirrored in light, here is where Diwali 2026 will be most spectacular — plus when to book before fares spike.
body:
• Diwali 2026 falls in early November, and for diaspora families planning a trip home, the festival rewards picking the right city: Varanasi for spirituality, Jaipur for spectacle, Amritsar for the Golden Temple at its most luminous.
  • Varanasi's Dev Deepawali — the "Diwali of the gods" on Kartik Purnima, about two weeks after Diwali — lights all 84 ghats with a million diyas and is arguably the grander sight.
  • Airfares from the US typically run 25% to 40% above off-peak around Diwali, so booking two to four months ahead is the single biggest money-saver.
  • Regional traditions vary widely: Kolkata worships Kali rather than Lakshmi, Goa burns giant demon effigies for Naraka Chaturdashi, and Ayodhya stages a world-record diya lighting.

If you are planning a trip to India for Diwali this year, the question is not whether to go — it is where to be when the lamps are lit. The festival of lights falls in early November 2026, and different cities offer radically different Diwalis: a spiritual one on the Ganges, a royal one in Rajasthan, a luminous one at the Golden Temple. Here is where the festival is at its most unforgettable.

Varanasi: the spiritual epicenter

No city does Diwali quite like Varanasi. Thousands of diyas line the ghats along the Ganges, the Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat takes on a grander scale, and fireworks bloom over the river while boats drift past lamp-lit steps. Come hungry: the festive season brings out local sweets like malaiyo and jalebi. And if your dates are flexible, consider timing the trip for Dev Deepawali — the "Diwali of the gods" on Kartik Purnima, about two weeks after Diwali — when all 84 ghats are illuminated with a reported million earthen lamps in a single evening.

Jaipur: the Pink City turned golden

Jaipur may be the most photogenic Diwali in India. Entire markets glow — Johari Bazaar, famously dubbed "the strip" after its Las Vegas namesake for its wall of light, anchors the spectacle — while the City Palace, Hawa Mahal and Nahargarh Fort are illuminated against the night sky. Days are for the bazaars (Johari and Bapu for handicrafts and festive shopping) and the food: ghevar and dal baati churma are non-negotiable.

Amritsar: Diwali meets Bandi Chhor Divas

In Amritsar, Diwali coincides with the Sikh festival of Bandi Chhor Divas, marking Guru Hargobind Ji's release from imprisonment — and the Golden Temple, bathed in lights with its reflection shimmering on the sarovar beneath a fireworks-lit sky, is one of the great sights of the Indian festival calendar. The city's langars feed hundreds of thousands through the festivities, and the combined Hindu-Sikh celebration gives Amritsar's Diwali a character found nowhere else.

Elsewhere: Ayodhya, Kolkata, Goa, Delhi, Mumbai

Ayodhya — regarded as Lord Rama's birthplace and the mythological home of Diwali itself — now stages a world-record lighting of diyas each year. In Kolkata, the festival takes a different form entirely: the fearsome goddess Kali is worshipped instead of Lakshmi, oil lamps on tall poles are lit to guide departed souls, and towering images of the "Dark Mother" appear across the city. Goa marks Naraka Chaturdashi with giant demon effigies set ablaze to celebrate good's triumph over evil. Delhi counters with Ramlila grounds fielding 100-foot-plus Ravan effigies and the Akshardham light show; Mumbai answers with fireworks over Marine Drive.

Planning it: fares, booking and practical tips

The unglamorous part matters most. Airfare to India from the US around Diwali typically runs 25% to 40% above off-peak months, according to travel planners — booking two to four months ahead is the single biggest lever on price, with last-minute October bookings the most expensive. Hotels in Varanasi and Amritsar fill fast for the festival week; reserve early and confirm festival-night availability in writing.

On the ground: carry light woolens for North India's cool November nights, keep cash handy for small vendors and rural markets, give fireworks a wide berth in crowded areas, and respect local custom — remove footwear before entering homes and temples, dress modestly, and observe quiet during evening pujas. Families performing rituals often welcome respectful visitors who ask first; lighting a diya or trying your hand at rangoli is the fastest way to be adopted for the evening.
